extracted.intended_audience: industry data scientists and reviewers conducting peer reviews of data-science projects
extracted.subtask_description: A two-phase framework for performing peer review of industry data science work: an early research-phase review that checks methodology selection and approach viability, followed by a model-development review focused on implementation and model performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research-phase review
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodology selection and approach viability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary early-stage review phase intended to evaluate whether the proposed research approach is viable before substantial implementation effort. Encompasses preparation, a ≥60 minute meeting, checklist examination, and an approval/rejection decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model-development review
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation and model performance review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second phase of review focused on implementation correctness, model behavior, and production-readiness. Uses a separate checklist covering data assumptions, preprocessing, leakage, causality, evaluation, overfitting, runtime, and common implementation errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation: reviewed scientist deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewed scientist prepares scope, KPIs, assumptions, data exploration, possible approaches, recommendation, contingency plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer expects a package that clearly states scope and objectives (KPIs), enumerates key assumptions, summarizes exploratory data analysis, outlines candidate approaches and a recommended approach, and includes contingency plans if the preferred approach fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting length requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Meeting ≥60 min.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research-phase review should allow at least 60 minutes for presentation, discussion, checklist walk-through, and decision; implies time allocation for substantive critique and follow-up assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer pre-meeting study
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer studies the checklist beforehand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer should review the prepared materials and checklist in advance so the meeting time is used for focused discussion rather than orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation by reviewed scientist; general feedback from reviewer; checklist examination; approval/rejection decision; action items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structured meeting sequence: (1) reviewed scientist presents their plan, (2) reviewer provides high-level feedback, (3) both examine checklist items in detail, (4) reviewer issues approval or rejection for the approach, (5) define concrete action items for next steps or remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval / rejection decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision at end of research-phase meeting to approve or reject the proposed approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer must make and record a clear decision on whether to proceed with the recommended approach; approval may be conditional on action items, rejection should include reasons and next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action items / follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Define action items after the review meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List concrete tasks, owners, and deadlines to address concerns, implement recommended changes, or proceed to model development; ensures accountability and fixes before implementation proceeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate sampling, bias, and representativeness of the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the dataset adequately represents the problem population, identify sampling biases, class imbalance, and any issues that would limit generalizability. Examine how data collection choices affect downstream validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess validity of approach assumptions and behavior on edge cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit all assumptions (statistical, causal, business) and probe where they may fail. Consider edge cases and robustness: when do assumptions break, and what are impacts on KPIs?

rubrics_metrics.name: Past experience / precedents
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider relevant prior experience and precedents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage lessons learned from similar projects, known pitfalls, and past empirical results to judge feasibility and likely failure modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective alignment (loss functions vs. KPIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure chosen loss functions and evaluation objectives align with business KPIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that model optimization targets meaningful business outcomes; avoid optimizing proxies that do not reflect success metrics. Discuss metrics selection and tradeoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation considerations (tools, support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess implementation tools and support requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether proposed tooling, platforms, and engineering support exist or can be procured; consider maintainability, reproducibility, and operational constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaling (computational requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate computational requirements and scalability of the approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate compute, storage, and runtime costs for training and serving at production scale; assess feasibility and cost-effectiveness when scaled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composability (modularity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess modularity and composability of the approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer modular designs that allow components to be replaced or reused; consider integration with existing pipelines and future extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information requirements (data sufficiency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether available data is sufficient for the intended approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check sample size, feature quality, label reliability, and whether additional data collection is required. Consider active learning or data augmentation where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain adaptation (cold-start)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider domain adaptation challenges and cold-start scenarios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how models will perform when domain shifts occur, and plan for cold-start situations (e.g., new users, new locales). Include strategies for transfer learning or bootstrapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noise and bias resilience
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess robustness to noise and biases in data and labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine susceptibility to noisy labels, adversarial inputs, and systemic bias; plan mitigation techniques such as robust loss functions, debiasing, or better data collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model-development checklist (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate checklist used during model-development review covering implementation and validation details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model-development reviews focus on concrete technical evaluation: verifying data assumptions, preprocessing correctness, leakage detection, causal reasoning, metric choice, overfitting detection, runtime characteristics, and common implementation errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model-development: data assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-check and validate data assumptions during implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that assumptions made during research-phase hold in practice (e.g., stationarity, independence). Re-run explorations on processed datasets to detect surprises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model-development: preprocessing
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspect preprocessing steps for correctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify feature engineering, scaling, encoding, missing-value handling, leakage-prone transformations, and that preprocessing is consistently applied between training and serving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model-development: leakage detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect and prevent data leakage between training and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for label leakage, temporal leakage, or cross-contamination between train/validation/test splits. Ensure evaluation mimics production conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model-development: causality
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider causal relationships and whether correlations are spurious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether model decisions rely on causal mechanisms or spurious correlations; where causal inference is required, assess identification strategy and sensitivity to confounders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model-development: evaluation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Review chosen evaluation metrics for appropriateness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure metrics reflect business KPIs and capture relevant errors (e.g., precision/recall tradeoffs, calibration). Use suitable validation schemes and baseline comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model-development: overfitting detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect signs of overfitting and poor generalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare training vs. validation performance, use cross-validation where appropriate, and inspect learning curves. Consider regularization, simpler models, or more data if overfitting detected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model-development: runtime
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess runtime and operational performance constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure inference latency, throughput, resource utilization, and reproducibility. Ensure model meets production SLAs or outline necessary engineering changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model-development: common implementation errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Check for typical implementation mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for bugs in data pipelines, label mismatches, incorrect metric calculations, improper use of random seeds, non-deterministic behaviors, and issues that invalidate experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core motivation / risk rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Rationale that approach failures are very costly when discovered late; early scrutiny prevents deploying flawed models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as overarching justification for performing two-phase reviews and enforcing preparation and checklists: catching methodological flaws early saves time and prevents costly production failures.
